question: What rebates are available for a heat pump?
html:
We don't have a verified, current list of heat pump rebates, so we won't quote programs or dollar amounts. What you can get depends on your utility, your zip code and how you heat today. A technician can check the programs that apply to your home before you commit.

What sets your rebate

  • Your electric utility. Utility programs differ by service area, so your zip code matters.
  • Your current heating fuel. Some programs treat replacing oil or propane differently from replacing gas or electric resistance heat.
  • The equipment and installer. Many programs require qualifying efficiency ratings or approved contractors.
  • Timing. Programs open, close and change funding, so any list goes out of date quickly.

How homes here heat

Many homes in our area still use oil or propane (Punctual Pros market profile, based on Census ACS 2020-2024 data):

AreaHomes on oil or propane
Perry County44.5%
Lebanon County37.6%
Berks County30.0%
Adams County27.7%
Lancaster County25.2%
Ocean and Monmouth, NJ78-81% use utility gas
  • That is about 241k households across our nine-county Central PA core.
  • Between 45% and 64% of homes in our area were built before 1980. Older systems often need a full assessment before any upgrade.

What to have ready

  • Your zip code and electric utility.
  • What heats your home now, and the age of the system.
  • Your goal: replacing failed equipment or planning an upgrade.

We can then check which programs apply and what paperwork they need. We can't advise on tax or legal eligibility. For tax credits, talk to your tax preparer.

Data that would answer this

  • A rebate table for each utility in our service area, matched to zip codes and checked every month.
  • Current state program status for Pennsylvania and New Jersey.
  • Any manufacturer or brand promotions running this season.

Clear rebate answers turn the large base of oil and propane homes into booked heat pump installs, so this page decides whether a curious visitor becomes a lead.

Next actions for the operating team

  1. Build and own a utility rebate table matched to zip codes for Pennsylvania and New Jersey. Assign one owner and set a monthly review date.
  2. Add a "check my rebates" form that captures zip code, heating fuel and system age, then routes the lead to dispatch.
  3. Prioritize outreach in Perry, Lebanon, Berks, Adams and Lancaster, where oil and propane shares are highest (Punctual Pros market profile).
  4. Train technicians and call staff to log each customer's current fuel. Over time, this measures heat pump conversion demand directly instead of relying on estimates.
